text.p: Portuguese bonds closed lower but recouped some earlier losses in line with Spanish Bonos after news Russian president Boris Yeltsin fired his security chief.

Dealers said concern that Spain and Italy might not join the European Union's single currency from the outset would keep investors wary of the Portuguese market, but the stronger dollar could lend Iberian markets some support.
"The market regained its composure this afternoon after a jittery morning dominated by worries about the euro," said one trader. "If Spain heads higher tomorrow we should follow suit," he added.
Alexander Lebed's dismissal pushed the escudo up slightly against a falling mark and currency traders thought the currency would make further gains on Friday.
The escudo closed at 100.77/80 per mark, up from an opening 100.82/85.
In quiet money market trading overnight/tomorrow next rates were barely changed at 7.05/7.15 percent.
